html:
The map's 1715 snapshot gives the old name Tekrur to the middle Senegal River valley, in what is now northern Senegal. The medieval kingdom of Takrur had stood here; by 1715 the land was called Futa Toro and was ruled by the Denianke, a Fula dynasty founded by Koli Tenguella around 1500.

The Denianke kings, called satigi, ruled a land of farmers who planted the river floodplain as the water fell, and of Fula herders. The valley was squeezed between Moorish emirates to the north, which raided it, and the French trading post at Saint-Louis at the river's mouth, which bought gum arabic and slaves.

Muslim scholars, the Torodbe, resented the Denianke as lax rulers. In 1776 they overthrew them and set up the Islamic Imamate of Futa Toro, one of the West African jihad states, like Futa Jallon before it.
